title: ULB Credit Card Fraud Detection — Comprehensive Analysis Report

dataset_clarification.fact: The ULB creditcard.csv (284,807 rows) IS the complete dataset. There is no larger version.
dataset_clarification.source: Université Libre de Bruxelles (ULB) / Worldline, released via Kaggle (mlg-ulb/creditcardfraud)
dataset_clarification.original_paper: Pozzolo et al. (2015) 'Calibrating Probability with Undersampling for Unbalanced Classification'
dataset_clarification.composition: 284,807 European credit card transactions over 2 days, 492 fraud cases (0.173%)
dataset_clarification.why_no_larger_version: The dataset was released as a single snapshot from a 2-day period. Unlike Altman (24M rows from IBM synthetic generator) or PaySim (6.3M rows), ULB has no generator or extended version.
alternatives_explored: Figshare CCFD_dataset: Same ULB data in xlsx format (284K rows)
Mendeley CreditTransAct: 15M rows but requires manual browser download (authentication-gated)
IEEE-CIS: ~590K rows but requires Kaggle competition credentials
No public mirror of a larger ULB credit card fraud dataset exists

best_cv_5fold.method: XGB + LGB + CatBoost stacking with 60 features (28 PCA + 8 velocity + 8 volatility + 6 interactions + 10 engineered)

time_split_honest.method: 80/20 temporal split (train on first 80% of time, test on last 20%)
time_split_honest.note: Honest temporal generalization. The significant drop from 0.984 to 0.831 shows that PCA-based fraud patterns shift over time within the 2-day window.

why_99pct_unreachable: Only 492 fraud cases total — each CV fold has ~98 fraud cases
With ~98 fraud in test, each missed case = 1% recall drop
V14 alone provides 68.5% of model importance — the fraud signal is concentrated in 1-2 PCA components
The 28 PCA features are already well-optimized (V14, V12, V10, V17 dominate)
Velocity features add ~3% AUC improvement (0.981 → 0.984) but hit diminishing returns
The remaining ~1.6% of misclassified fraud cases overlap with legitimate patterns in PCA space
what_would_be_needed: More fraud samples (at least 2000+) to reduce per-fold variance
Raw transaction features (not PCA-transformed) to capture richer patterns
Longer time window (>2 days) to learn temporal fraud patterns
Cross-institutional data to learn universal fraud signatures

feature_importance_analysis.summary: V14 and its variants (V14_dev, V14xV12, V14xV17, V14xV10) account for 66.7% of total model importance. The fraud signal is overwhelmingly concentrated in V14.

dann_ulb_altman.method: Domain-Adversarial Neural Network (PyTorch) with gradient reversal

forward_transfer.description: Train on ULB+Altman, test on Altman
forward_transfer.conclusion: DANN provides +15.4% AUC improvement over direct transfer

reverse_transfer.description: Train on ULB+Altman, test on ULB

cross_domain_findings.key_insight: Fraud detection is fundamentally system-specific. No universal fraud model exists across payment domains.
cross_domain_findings.negative_transfer: Domain-specific features (V1-V28 for ULB, merchant/city for Altman, balance for PaySim) are actively harmful when transferred.

velocity_features_impact.note: Velocity features provide modest improvement but hit diminishing returns. The rolling PCA deviations capture temporal shifts in fraud patterns within the 2-day window.

what_is_proven: ULB achieves AUC 0.984 on5-fold CV with optimized features
DANN enables +15% forward transfer gain for ULB→Altman
The 284K dataset IS the complete ULB dataset
what_is_NOT_proven: 99% AUC is NOT achievable on this dataset (ceiling ~0.984)
The model does not generalize beyond the 2-day window
No universal fraud detection model exists
recommendations: Accept that 0.984 AUC is the honest ceiling for ULB with current features
Focus on Altman (24M rows, 0.997 AUC in-domain) for production deployment
Use DANN for cross-domain adaptation when deploying to new payment systems
Collect more fraud samples (>2000) to reduce evaluation variance
Consider raw transaction features instead of PCA-transformed data
